issues.description: The problem text explicitly instructs that the Animal.name attribute should use StringBuilder for efficient modifications, but the solution implementation (Animal.java) defines the name field as a String. This mismatch between the specification and the reference implementation can confuse students about which type to use and may cause grading/tests to expect different behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Reconcile the specification and the implementation. Either update the solution (and any template/test expectations) so Animal.name is a StringBuilder and adjust getter/setter accordingly, or change the problem statement to require a String for the name attribute. Preferably, update the solution to use StringBuilder to match the explicit textual requirement.

issues.description: Within the problem statement itself, the UML diagram shows Animal.name as type String, while the textual instructions explicitly require StringBuilder for the name attribute. This internal contradiction can confuse students about which type the UML or the text should be followed.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the problem statement internally consistent: update the UML diagram to show the name attribute as StringBuilder, or remove the textual instruction about StringBuilder and keep String in the UML. Explicitly state which representation students should follow.
